concepts.name: Establishment and Evolution of MoEFCC
key_dimensions: Historical evolution: from Department of Environment (1980) → Ministry of Environment & Forests (1985) → MoEFCC (2014) — year traps
Trigger for 'CC' addition: Paris Agreement negotiations and India's climate diplomacy context
Institutional distinction from CPCB, NGCT, and other bodies under vs. alongside MoEFCC
UPSC trap: MoEFCC is an executive ministry, NOT a statutory body — its powers derive from Acts, not its own constitution

concepts.name: MoEFCC as Nodal Ministry: Scope and Boundaries
key_dimensions: Nodal ministry for UN conventions: UNFCCC, CBD, CITES, Ramsar, Basel, Stockholm, Minamata — which conventions fall under MoEFCC vs. other ministries
Overlap trap: Climate finance under MoF, disaster risk under MHA, ocean governance shared with MoES
Role in coordinating India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) vs. actual implementation by other ministries
UPSC trap: MoEFCC is nodal for UNFCCC but Ministry of New & Renewable Energy handles solar/wind targets

concepts.name: Environmental Clearance (EC) Process under EIA Notification 2006
key_dimensions: Four-stage EC process: Screening → Scoping → Public Consultation → Appraisal — and which stages are skipped for Category B2 projects
Category A (MoEFCC) vs. Category B (SEIAA) jurisdiction — the critical threshold distinction
Public hearing exemption list: strategic/defence projects, small industries in notified industrial areas — UPSC favourite exception area
Controversy: EIA Draft 2020 proposals (post-facto clearance, reduced public consultation) and SC/NGT pushback

concepts.name: Forest Clearance under Forest (Conservation) Act 1980
key_dimensions: Section 2 FCA: prior approval of Central Government for diversion of forest land — MoEFCC's gatekeeping role
Two-stage clearance: In-principle (Stage I) vs. Final (Stage II) — conditions and triggers for each
UPSC trap: FCA 1980 applies to 'forest land' as per records OR deemed forest (Godavarman judgment), not just notified forests
Forest Conservation Amendment Act 2023: exclusion of land within 100km of borders, private plantations — controversies and implications

concepts.name: MoEFCC's Role under Wildlife Protection Act 1972
key_dimensions: Central government powers: declaring National Parks, Tiger Reserves (in consultation with NTCA), Marine Protected Areas
UPSC trap: Sanctuaries can be declared by State governments; National Parks require Central approval — the critical distinction
Standing Committee of NBWL: composition, quorum requirements, and its role in clearing projects in eco-sensitive zones
Project Tiger and Project Elephant: administratively under MoEFCC but operationally through NTCA and Project Elephant Division

concepts.name: National Board for Wildlife (NBWL): Composition and Powers
key_dimensions: Statutory basis: Section 5A of WPA 1972 — chaired by Prime Minister (UPSC trap: NOT the Environment Minister)
Standing Committee chaired by Minister of Environment — often confused with full NBWL in exam questions
Powers: recommend policies, review and alter boundaries of PAs, grant permissions for projects in PAs/ESZs
UPSC trap: NBWL recommends; final notification of PA boundary changes still requires State government action for sanctuaries

concepts.name: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB): Relationship with MoEFCC
key_dimensions: Statutory basis: Section 3 of Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974 — CPCB is statutory, MoEFCC is executive
CPCB functions: coordinate SPCBs, advise Central Government, collect data — advisory NOT enforcement at state level
UPSC trap: CPCB cannot directly penalize industries — enforcement is with SPCBs; CPCB's directions bind SPCBs under Section 18
Hierarchy: CPCB under MoEFCC's administrative control but derives powers from Water Act and Air Act, not from MoEFCC orders

concepts.name: Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notifications: MoEFCC's Regulatory Role
key_dimensions: Legal basis: Environment Protection Act 1986, Section 3 — MoEFCC issues CRZ notifications as subordinate legislation
CRZ classification: CRZ-I (A&B), CRZ-II, CRZ-III (A&B), CRZ-IV — and permitted/prohibited activities in each zone
UPSC trap: CRZ 2019 replaced CRZ 2011 — key changes: No Development Zone reduced from 200m to 50m for densely populated areas
Island Protection Zone (IPZ) for A&N and Lakshadweep — separate from CRZ but also under MoEFCC's EPA powers

concepts.name: Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs): Declaration and Governance
key_dimensions: Legal basis: EPA 1986, Section 3 — MoEFCC notifies ESZs around Protected Areas as a 'shock absorber'
SC directions in T.N. Godavarman case: mandatory 10km ESZ around every PA — MoEFCC's compliance obligations
UPSC trap: ESZ notification is by MoEFCC (Central), but monitoring and enforcement involves State governments and District Collectors
Activities classification in ESZs: prohibited (mining, industries), regulated (tourism, felling), permitted (ongoing agriculture) — trap in 'only' questions

concepts.name: Hazardous Waste Management: MoEFCC's Rule-Making Power
key_dimensions: Legal chain: EPA 1986 → Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules 2016 — MoEFCC as rule-maker
Basel Convention implementation in India: MoEFCC as nodal ministry for transboundary movement of hazardous waste
UPSC trap: E-waste rules, plastic waste rules, biomedical waste rules — all under EPA 1986 but notified by MoEFCC, enforced by SPCBs
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR): MoEFCC's policy role vs. CPCB's implementation/registration role — frequent confusion

concepts.name: Biological Diversity Act 2002: MoEFCC and NBA Relationship
key_dimensions: Three-tier structure: NBA (national) → SBBs (state) → BMCs (local) — MoEFCC's role in establishing and overseeing NBA
UPSC trap: NBA is a statutory body under BDA 2002, NOT under MoEFCC's direct control — it has autonomous status
Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS): MoEFCC's role in Nagoya Protocol implementation vs. NBA's operational role
Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023: exemptions for AYUSH sector, codified traditional knowledge — MoEFCC-driven amendment controversy

concepts.name: Climate Change Governance: MoEFCC's Role vs. Other Ministries
key_dimensions: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC): MoEFCC coordinates 8 missions but implementing ministries are different (e.g., MNRE for solar, Jal Shakti for water)
UPSC trap: National Mission for Green India (GIM) is under MoEFCC; National Solar Mission is under MNRE — classic confusion
State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs): States prepare, MoEFCC approves — the approval architecture
India's NDC submission to UNFCCC: MoEFCC prepares, Cabinet approves — distinction between policy formulation and diplomatic submission

concepts.name: Environment Protection Act 1986: MoEFCC as Umbrella Authority
key_dimensions: Section 3: Central Government (exercised through MoEFCC) can take 'all measures' — sweeping delegated power, not specific enumeration
Section 5: Power to issue directions to any person/officer/authority — binding directions including closure, prohibition
UPSC trap: EPA 1986 is the 'umbrella act' — all rules (CRZ, EIA, Hazardous Waste) derive from it, but Water Act (1974) and Air Act (1981) are independent statutes
Section 19: Cognizance of offences only on complaint by Central/State Government or approved persons — bars private criminal complaints (important procedural trap)

concepts.name: National Green Tribunal (NGT): MoEFCC's Position Before It
key_dimensions: UPSC trap: NGT is NOT under MoEFCC — it is an independent statutory tribunal under NGT Act 2010, under administrative control of MoLJ
MoEFCC as a frequent respondent before NGT, not its parent ministry — the power inversion dynamic
NGT jurisdiction over 7 scheduled Acts: includes EPA, Water Act, Air Act, FCA, BDA, WPA, Public Liability Insurance Act
UPSC trap: NGT cannot hear matters under Wildlife Protection Act 1972 in all cases — limited to specific scheduled provisions

concepts.name: Forest Survey of India (FSI) and Wildlife Institute of India (WII): Subordinate Bodies
key_dimensions: FSI: statutory/non-statutory status (it is a subordinate office, NOT a statutory body) — publishes biennial India State of Forest Report (ISFR)
UPSC trap: FSI defines forest cover based on satellite imagery of canopy density ≥10% — includes plantations, NOT the same as 'forest' under FCA 1980
WII: autonomous institution under MoEFCC — wildlife research, capacity building; distinct from NTCA which is statutory
ICFRE (Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education): apex body for forestry research under MoEFCC — often confused with FSI in exam options

concepts.name: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA): Powers and MoEFCC Oversight
key_dimensions: Statutory basis: WPA 1972 (amended 2006), Section 38L — NTCA chaired by Minister of Environment (UPSC trap: NOT PM, unlike NBWL)
NTCA powers: approve Tiger Conservation Plans, provide grants, regulate tourism in core/buffer zones
UPSC trap: Tiger Reserves have Core (Critical Tiger Habitat) and Buffer zones — Core notified by State government with NTCA approval, not by MoEFCC directly
Project Tiger: launched 1973, predates NTCA (2006) — administrative history and shift from project-mode to statutory authority

concepts.name: Compensatory Afforestation: CAMPA and MoEFCC's Role
key_dimensions: Legal evolution: SC orders (2002) → CAMPA Act 2016 — MoEFCC's role in framing rules and overseeing National CAMPA Authority
Fund flow: User agencies deposit → Ad-hoc CAMPA (earlier, SC-monitored) → State CAMPAs — MoEFCC's oversight architecture
UPSC trap: Net Present Value (NPV) and Compensatory Afforestation are both levied on forest diversion but serve different purposes — NPV for ecological services, CA for physical afforestation
2:1 ratio rule: non-forest land for CA vs. degraded forest land (1:2) — and MoEFCC's role in verifying compliance

concepts.name: International Conventions: MoEFCC as Nodal Ministry vs. Coordinator
key_dimensions: UPSC trap matrix: UNFCCC (MoEFCC), CBD (MoEFCC), CITES (MoEFCC), Ramsar (MoEFCC), Basel (MoEFCC) — but Rotterdam Convention (MoC+MoEFCC jointly), Minamata (MoEFCC)
Paris Agreement: ratified by India in 2016 — MoEFCC leads negotiations but NDC implementation is cross-ministerial
CITES implementation in India: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) under MoEFCC is the enforcement arm — distinction between nodal and enforcement bodies
UPSC trap: Ramsar Convention wetland designation — MoEFCC nominates, Ramsar Secretariat lists; MoEFCC does NOT have unilateral power to de-list

concepts.name: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA): Exemptions and Special Categories
key_dimensions: Projects exempted from EIA entirely: modernization of irrigation projects, highway projects less than 100km in non-sensitive areas — trap in 'which requires EC' questions
Strategic projects: defence and national security projects can get exemption from public consultation — MoEFCC's discretionary power
UPSC trap: Linear projects (roads, pipelines) in forests require BOTH Forest Clearance (FCA) AND Environmental Clearance (EPA) — not either/or
Deemed EC lapse: if construction begins before EC or EC conditions violated — MoEFCC's power to revoke vs. NGT's power to stay

concepts.name: Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017: MoEFCC's Regulatory Framework
key_dimensions: Shift from Wetlands Rules 2010: 2017 rules devolved authority to State Wetland Authorities — MoEFCC's role reduced to oversight and policy
UPSC trap: Ramsar sites have an additional layer — activities near Ramsar sites need compliance with both Wetlands Rules 2017 AND Ramsar guidelines
Prohibited activities in wetlands: solid waste dumping, construction, reclamation — enforced by State authorities, NOT directly by MoEFCC
National Wetland Conservation Programme (NWCP): centrally sponsored scheme under MoEFCC — funding architecture and identification of wetlands of national importance
